object_description: two elongated motorway-oriented volumes with longitudinal gable roofs
design_condition: The two volumes are oriented toward the motorway while infrastructure follows the historic eastern axis, but the first-stage arrangement leaves a noise-exposed open space and a public access axis terminating in a gated service zone.

positive.statement: The carefully coordinated roof landscape contributes to fundamentally good integration into the landscape.

position.rationale: Paired elongated roof forms and their coordinated footprint are clearly visible across top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The separation of staff and visitor entrances is correct for distinguishing staff and goods flows.

position.rationale: Entrances are not distinguishable, so the marker approximates an accessible end of the paired volumes.

positive.statement: The structural concept is sophisticated and the timber construction is sustainable.

position.rationale: Structure is not individually sampled; placement is constrained to the visible upper-volume envelope.

positive.statement: The carefully formulated facade creates a coherent ensemble despite differing functions.

position.rationale: Repeated parallel facade bands visibly unify the two elongated volumes despite their separation.

positive.statement: The lightweight structural concept promises relatively cost-effective implementation.

position.rationale: The structural system is not individually visible; marker is placed on the sampled lightweight volume envelope.

positive.statement: The internal organization works and is largely well organized within the two volumes.

position.rationale: Interior layout is absent, so the marker covers a plausible region within the paired massing.

negative.statement: If only the first stage is implemented, the structure is positioned suboptimally and creates a large noise-polluted space.

position.target: first-stage structure and noise-polluted open space
position.rationale: The exposed intermediate gap between the two sampled volumes is visible in the top view.

negative.statement: The east-west access axis ends in an infrastructure zone inaccessible to the public and closed with gates.

position.target: east-west access axis and gated infrastructure zone
position.rationale: The infrastructure endpoint is not identifiable; marker approximates a peripheral access termination.

negative.statement: Dividing the program into two volumes requires many functional connections through the only partly covered intermediate space.

position.rationale: The partly covered intermediate space is represented by the visible separation between parallel volumes.

negative.statement: The arrangement of the studios and workshops in the covered space is called into question.

position.target: studios and workshops in covered space
position.rationale: Studios and workshops are not distinguishable; marker approximates the central covered gap.

negative.statement: The concept is unspecific and more reminiscent of agricultural buildings than of the intended collection center.

position.rationale: The paired low-rise elongated gabled masses visibly support the stated agricultural-building association.

negative.statement: The internal organization cannot be optimally solved because of the building shape and division into two volumes.

position.target: internal organization constrained by building division
position.rationale: Interior constraints are not sampled; placement spans a plausible region of one elongated volume.
